questions.question: Let $L[x]=x^{(n)}+a_{n-1}x^{(n-1)}+\dots+a_1x'+a_0x$ be a linear differential operator and $g\not\equiv0$ a forcing term. If $x_{p,1}$ and $x_{p,2}$ both satisfy $L[x]=g$ on an interval, which equation does the difference $x_{p,1}-x_{p,2}$ satisfy there?
options: No equation: the difference is identically $0$

questions.question: Let $L[x]=x^{(n)}+a_{n-1}x^{(n-1)}+\dots+a_1x'+a_0x$ be a linear differential operator. Suppose $L[x_1]=g_1$ and $L[x_2]=g_2$ on an interval. Which function satisfies $L[x]=g_1-3g_2$ there?

In the method of undetermined coefficients for a constant-coefficient equation $L[x]=g$, a trial function $\phi$ is chosen of the same type as $g$. Why must $\phi$ be multiplied by $t$ when $\phi$ itself solves $L[x]=0$?
options: Because then $L[A\phi]=0$ for every $A$, so matching gives $0=g$
Because a homogeneous trial makes $x_p$ grow too fast
Because the factor $t$ is needed for any exponential forcing

questions.question: The method of undetermined coefficients guesses a trial function of the same type as the forcing $g$ and matches terms. For which of these equations, in the unknown $x(t)$ on $t>0$, is it NOT applicable as it stands?

For the inhomogeneous linear equation $L[x]=g$ of order $n$ with $g\not\equiv0$, considered on an interval $I$, which condition is both necessary and sufficient for a function $x_p$ to be a particular solution?
options: $x_p$ satisfies $L[x_p]=0$ and is not identically zero
$x_p$ is the only function with $L[x_p]=g$ on $I$

questions.question: Find a constant particular solution of $x''+3x'+2x=6$, where $x=x(t)$.
Find a particular solution of $x''-3x'+2x=4\mathrm{e}^{3t}$, whose characteristic polynomial is $p(r)=r^2-3r+2$.
For the first-order equation $x'+2x=4t$, the trial $x_p=At+B$ is used. Which particular solution results?
Find a particular solution of $x''+4x=3\sin t$ using the trial $x_p=A\sin t$.
For $x''+x'-2x=\mathrm{e}^{t}$, with characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^2+r-2=(r-1)(r+2)$, which trial function should the method of undetermined coefficients use?
Consider $x'+p(t)x=q(t)$ with $p,q$ continuous on an interval $I$ and $p$ not constant. Which approach is guaranteed to produce a particular solution on $I$?
options: Guess a function of the same type as $q$

questions.question: For the constant-coefficient equation $x''+2x'+5x=\cos t$, the method of undetermined coefficients is used. Why does the trial $A\cos t$ fail, so that $A\cos t+B\sin t$ is needed?
options: Because $\pm i$ are roots of $r^2+2r+5$, so $\cos t$ resonates
Because $\sin t$ is needed to make the particular solution real
Because $2x'$ produces a $\sin t$ term that must also be matched
Because a second-order equation needs two unknown coefficients

questions.question: The equation $x''+9x=g(t)$ has characteristic roots $\pm3i$. For which forcing $g$ must the trial function of the method of undetermined coefficients be multiplied by $t$?
For $x''+3x'+2x=4t$ (characteristic roots $-1$ and $-2$), $x_p=2t-3$ is a particular solution. Which other function is also a particular solution of this equation?
Find a particular solution of $x''+3x'=6$, whose characteristic polynomial $r^2+3r$ has the root $0$.
In $x''-4x=8\mathrm{e}^{2t}$ the exponent $2$ of the forcing is a simple root of $p(r)=r^2-4$. Which function satisfies the equation?
Claim: \"For constant-coefficient $L[x]=k\mathrm{e}^{st}$ with $k\neq0$, whenever $p(s)=0$ the trial $At\mathrm{e}^{st}$ yields a particular solution.\" Which assessment is correct?
options: True: one factor $t$ always removes the resonance
False: it works when $s$ is a simple root, not a repeated one
False: when $p(s)=0$ no particular solution exists at all
False: the trial should be $(A+Bt)\mathrm{e}^{st}$ in every case

questions.question: For $\boldsymbol{x}'=A\boldsymbol{x}+\boldsymbol{b}$ with constant $\boldsymbol{b}$, the constant $\boldsymbol{x}_p=-A^{-1}\boldsymbol{b}$ is a particular solution when $A$ is invertible. What can go wrong if $A$ is singular?
options: Nothing: a constant solution exists for every $A$
Then no particular solution of any kind exists
No constant solution may exist, e.g. $x'=0\cdot x+1$

questions.question: For $x''+ax'+bx=g(t)$ with real constants $a,b$, both $x_{p,1}=t+\mathrm{e}^{2t}$ and $x_{p,2}=t$ are particular solutions. Which condition on $a$ and $b$ must hold?
Find a particular solution of $x''+3x'+2x=2+\mathrm{e}^{-t}$; the characteristic polynomial $p(r)=r^2+3r+2$ has roots $-1$ and $-2$.
